name: Bouteloua

project_scope.note: B002 established the original four-species comparison set; B078 added B. hirsuta, B. pectinata, and B. trifida. The older source name Bouteloua hirsuta var. pectinata is represented by canonical B. pectinata rather than duplicated.

shared_traits: inflorescences built from short unilateral spicate branches/racemes
spikelets arranged mainly along one side of each branch
narrow linear leaf blades typical of Chloridoideae grasses
priority: branch length, width, curvature, and whether branches are appressed
whether branches are spaced down a long axis or clustered near the top
naked branch-tip projections beyond the spikelets
male versus female inflorescence differences in buffalograss
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Bouteloua from leaf color or overall 'grassiness.' Start with growth form and inflorescence architecture, then use branch-tip, awn, and hair characters.

quick_key.if: creeping stoloniferous sod; male and female inflorescences strongly different, with female clusters low and bur-like
many short oat-like racemes spaced down one side of a long central axis
tufted perennial; usually 1–4 comb-like branches and conspicuous papillose-based hairs near leaf bases; branch tip continues naked beyond terminal spikelets
taller, more robust hairy-grama relative with usually 3–5 longer straight to slightly curved combs, roughly 2.5–4.5 cm; old source names include B. hirsuta var./subsp. pectinata
about 5–9 very short fuzzy/awned branches clustered near the top
small wiry reddish plant with 2–7 narrow red/purplish branches held close to the main axis and three short awns on spikelets

fast_fill_note: FAST-FILL status: B. curtipendula 4; B. dactyloides 3; B. gracilis 3; B. hirsuta 3; B. trifida 2; B. rigidiseta 1; B. pectinata 0. Remaining gaps are source-limited presentation gaps, not scientific uncertainty. Do not substitute older varietal imagery for current B. pectinata without exact-concept verification.
taxonomy_note: Current Kew/POWO accepts Bouteloua pectinata Feath. as a species native from Oklahoma to Texas and Mexico. Older treatments use Bouteloua hirsuta var. pectinata or B. hirsuta subsp. pectinata; the project preserves those source names as aliases but uses one canonical B. pectinata learner.
